questions.question: A circle which passes through all three vertices of a triangle is called the:
questions.explanation: The circle circumscribing a triangle passes through all three vertices, and its centre is the circumcentre.

questions.question: The centre of a circumscribed circle (circumcentre) is the point of concurrency of the:

options.A: Right bisectors of the sides of the triangle
options.B: Internal bisectors of the angles of the triangle

questions.explanation: Perpendicular bisectors of the triangle's sides are concurrent at the circumcentre.

questions.question: A circle which touches all three sides of a triangle internally is called the:
questions.explanation: An incircle is drawn inside the triangle, tangent to all three sides.

questions.question: The centre of an inscribed circle (incentre) is the point of concurrency of the:

options.A: Internal bisectors of the angles of the triangle

questions.explanation: The internal angle bisectors meet at the incentre, which is equidistant from the three sides.

questions.question: A circle which touches one side of a triangle externally and the other two produced sides is called a/an:
questions.explanation: An excircle touches one side externally and two extended sides.

questions.question: How many escribed circles (excircles) can be drawn for any triangle?
questions.explanation: Every triangle has exactly three excircles, one opposite each of its three vertices.

questions.question: The centre of an escribed circle opposite to vertex A is the intersection of the:

options.A: Internal bisector of ∠A and external bisectors of ∠B and ∠C
options.B: External bisectors of all three angles

questions.explanation: The excentre I₁ is the concurrence point of the internal bisector of angle A and the external bisectors of angles B and C.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle, the circumcentre lies:

options.A: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse

questions.explanation: Because the hypotenuse subtends a 90° angle, it serves as diameter of the circumcircle; its midpoint is the circumcentre.

questions.question: In an obtuse-angled triangle, the circumcentre lies:
questions.explanation: For an obtuse triangle, the circumcentre falls outside the triangle opposite the obtuse angle.

questions.question: In an acute-angled triangle, the circumcentre lies:
questions.explanation: For all acute-angled triangles, the circumcentre lies strictly inside the triangle.

questions.question: The incentre of ANY triangle always lies:
questions.explanation: Because the incircle is enclosed within the three triangle sides, the incentre always lies strictly inside the triangle.

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle, the circumcentre, incentre, centroid, and orthocentre:

options.A: Coincide at the exact same point

questions.explanation: By perfect 3-fold symmetry, all four classical triangle centres coincide at one single point in an equilateral triangle.

questions.question: To draw a tangent to a circle from an external point P, we first construct a circle on line segment OP as:
questions.explanation: Using OP as diameter ensures that the inscribed angle at the circle's boundary is 90°, identifying the points of tangency.

questions.question: The radii of circumcircle R, incircle r, and excircles r₁, r₂, r₃ of an equilateral triangle of side 'a' satisfy the ratio:
questions.explanation: In an equilateral triangle, R = a/√3 and r = a/(2√3), giving the standard ratio r : R = 1 : 2.

questions.question: How many direct common tangents can be drawn to two separate non-intersecting circles?
questions.explanation: Two non-intersecting circles have 2 direct common tangents (and 2 transverse common tangents, totaling 4).

questions.question: How many transverse common tangents can be drawn to two separate non-intersecting circles?
questions.explanation: There are 2 transverse (internal crossing) common tangents between two separate disjoint circles.

questions.question: If two circles of equal radii touch externally, the transverse common tangent at the point of contact is:

options.A: Perpendicular to the line joining their centres
options.B: Parallel to the line of centres
options.C: At 45° to the line of centres
options.D: Coincident with the line of centres

questions.explanation: The line connecting centres is the common normal; the tangent at the contact point is perpendicular to it.

questions.question: The length of the transverse common tangent between two circles is:

options.A: Less than the length of the direct common tangent
options.B: Greater than the direct common tangent
options.C: Equal to the direct common tangent

questions.explanation: L_direct = √(d² - (r₁ - r₂)²), while L_transverse = √(d² - (r₁ + r₂)²). Since (r₁+r₂)² > (r₁-r₂)², transverse length is shorter.

questions.question: The radius of the incircle of a triangle with area Δ and semi-perimeter s is given by:
questions.explanation: The area of the triangle is the sum of three sub-triangles: Δ = 1/2 ar + 1/2 br + 1/2 cr = r(a+b+c)/2 = rs ⟹ r = Δ/s.

questions.question: The radius of an escribed circle touching side 'a' of a triangle is given by:
questions.explanation: By standard geometry formulas for excircles: r₁ = Δ / (s - a), r₂ = Δ / (s - b), and r₃ = Δ / (s - c).
